content.text:
The drawing shows a central CH2 carbon (the bend in the zigzag) with a "CN" label on one side and "Ts" on the other.

- Ts is tosyl, p-toluenesulfonyl: S(=O)(=O)c1ccc(C)cc1.
- The "CN" label is attached to the CH2 through its left-hand carbon, so I read it as a nitrile, C#N. The alternative reading, an isocyanide attached through nitrogen, would be drawn as "NC". The nitrile reading matches tosylacetonitrile, which is a common reagent.

The CH2 therefore carries the nitrile carbon and the sulfonyl group, giving N#CCS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(C)cc1.

SMILES: N#CCS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(C)cc1
